nodes.title: 🟨🌪️ CLIP Sub-Block Chaos Tuner ___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Perturbs chosen tensor families inside CLIP layers, to get a different reading of the same prompt.

HOW TO USE:
1. target_layer - a group or one single layer.
2. chaos_strength - keep it LOW here, 0.05-0.15. The text tower degrades much faster than the UNet.
3. Chance sliders (0.0-1.0) - probability per family. Start with the MLP ones.
4. seed - change it for a different interpretation; the same seed always reproduces.

WATCH OUT:
• Above roughly 0.20 the prompt stops being followed at all - that is the failure mode to expect, not blurry images.
• Perturbing ATTN_q_norm or NORMS_layernorm has an outsized effect: they are 1-D scales.

nodes.title: 🩷🔮 LoRA Block Loader ___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Loads a LoRA and lets you keep or drop it per group of blocks, instead of all-or-nothing.
• Groups: Text_Fusion, Time_Embed, Projection, Block_1..6 = blocks 0-4, 5-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20-23, 24-27.

HOW TO USE:
1. Pick 'lora_name' and set 'strength_model' / 'strength_clip' as usual.
2. Group sliders: 1.00 = that group at full LoRA strength, 0.00 = LoRA disabled there. Values in between scale it.
3. The two strengths multiply the group value, so 0.50 strength x 0.50 group = 0.25 in effect.

WHAT IT IS FOR:
• Keep a style LoRA only on the late blocks (Block_5-6) and its character bleed largely goes away.
• Keep it only on Block_1-2 and you get its composition without its surface.

WATCH OUT:
• Keys the group map does not recognise pass through at full strength - the info output warns if a LoRA matched 0 groups (usually a kohya-style naming this suite does not parse).
• LoRAs are NOT saved into presets. Use the Model Baker or Model Saver to make them permanent.

nodes.title: 🩷🌪️ Load Sub-Block Chaos LoRA ___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Loads a LoRA into a random subset of its tensors, so it blends in without the usual all-or-nothing LoRA signature.

HOW TO USE:
1. Pick 'lora_name' and 'target_block'.
2. 'base_chance' (default 0.20) - the probability applied to every family.
3. Per-family chance sliders override the base for that family.
4. seed - a different draw; same seed always reproduces.

WATCH OUT: the roll is once per module, so a LoRA's paired up/down tensors are never split. Low base_chance (0.15-0.30) is where this is useful; near 1.00 it is just the plain LoRA.

nodes.title: 🟪🟨🔄 Reset Patcher  ___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Drops every patch and Arthemy recipe pending on the model and CLIP, and rolls the patch id so ComfyUI restores any weight it had already modified in place.

HOW TO USE:
1. Place it right after your model and CLIP loaders.
2. Leave 'reset_model' / 'reset_clip' on True.
3. Its 'info' output reports how many patches and recipes it actually dropped, and says 'nothing was pending' when there was nothing to reset.

WATCH OUT:
• It clears only what this suite attached. Patches from other extensions (ModelSampling, FreeU) and hook-based LoRAs survive on purpose.
• It cannot undo a Model Baker: baked weights are the weights.

nodes.title: 🟪🟨💾 Preset Saver ___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Writes every active tuning into a .json preset: scalar and granular patches, plus reproducible recipes for Chaos, Rotations, Channel Magnitude and 5D.
• Saves to Arthemy_Krea2_Tuner/presets/ (or 'subfolder_or_path').

HOW TO USE:
1. Connect the tuned MODEL and CLIP. It saves even with outputs unconnected.
2. 'embed_5d_modifiers' ON = self-contained, reproduces anywhere. OFF = names the file only.
3. 'prune_5d_to_target' ON = embed only the layers the 5D nodes reach. Aimed at Block_3 the preset is ~6.5x smaller; at one tensor, ~48x.

WATCH OUT: LoRAs are excluded - bake them or save a full checkpoint.

nodes.title: 🩷🔬 Load Sub-Block LoRA ___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Loads a LoRA only into the tensor families you choose, inside the blocks you choose. Everything else of the LoRA is dropped.

HOW TO USE:
1. Pick 'lora_name', then 'target_block' (a group or one single block).
2. Family sliders: 1.00 = keep that part of the LoRA, 0.00 = drop it. In between scales it.
3. 'strength_model' / 'strength_clip' multiply on top.

WHAT IT IS FOR:
• Attention only = the LoRA's composition and framing, without its texture.
• MLP only = its surface and material, without its layout.

WATCH OUT: a LoRA only carries the tensors it was trained on. If a slider seems to do nothing, that family probably is not in the file - check the info output.

nodes.title: 🩷🟨🟪🧬 5D CLIP and Model Tuner _ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Injects a compressed LoRA back into the model or CLIP as a native low-rank patch, one SVD direction per slider - so you can use a fraction of a LoRA instead of the whole thing.

HOW TO USE:
1. 'source_lora' - a .json modifier from the Extractor, or a .safetensors LoRA (compressed on the fly and cached).
2. Dim_01..Dim_05 - the weight of each direction. Dim_01 is the strongest direction of the LoRA, Dim_05 the weakest of the five. 0.00 = off.
3. 'master_multiplier' scales all five at once.
4. 'target_block' / 'sub_components' / 'sub_tensor' - where to inject. The three intersect: leave sub_components on 'All Components' when you use sub_tensor.

HOW TO EXPLORE IT:
Fix the seed. Set Dim_01 = 1.00, everything else 0, and generate. Then Dim_02 alone. One direction at a time is the only way to learn what each one carries; all five at once is just the LoRA back.

WATCH OUT:
• A LoRA only carries the tensors it was trained on: norm/mod entries usually have no up/down pair, and a fused QKV cannot be split into WQ/WK/WV.
• The narrower the targeting, the smaller the preset - the Preset Saver embeds only the layers this selection reaches.

nodes.title: 🟨✨ CLIP Tuner ___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Scales the text encoder (Qwen3-VL) one layer group at a time.
• Embedding = the token embedding table. Layer_1..7 = text layers 0-4, 5-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20-24, 25-29, 30-35.

HOW TO USE:
1. mode - 'Soft Value' damps the slider to 10% (1.00 -> x1.10); 'Real Value' is 1:1. Keep Soft here, the text tower is far less forgiving than the UNet.
2. Sliders: 0.00 = untouched. Small moves first: +/-0.20 is already visible.
3. Generate with a fixed seed and compare prompt adherence, not aesthetics.

WHAT EACH GROUP DOES:
• Layer_1-2 (0-9): tokens, syntax, literal wording.
• Layer_3-5 (10-24): relations, attributes, who-does-what.
• Layer_6-7 (25-35): register, style, overall intent.

WATCH OUT:
• The vision tower (indices 36-59) is NOT touched by these sliders - it only runs when you feed reference images to the Krea2 text encoder.
• 'vectors_override' takes exactly 8 comma-separated values (Embedding + 7 groups).
• Push a group past about +1.00 in Real Value and the prompt starts to fall apart.

nodes.title: 🟪✨ Model Tuner ___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Scales whole groups of the diffusion model by a single multiplier each.
• Groups: Text_Fusion, Time_Embed, Projection, and Block_1..6 = blocks 0-4, 5-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20-23, 24-27.

HOW TO USE:
1. mode - 'Soft Value' damps the slider to 10% (1.00 -> x1.10). 'Real Value' is 1:1 (1.00 -> x2.00). Start Soft.
2. Sliders: 0.00 = untouched. Positive strengthens the group, negative weakens it.
3. Read 'Patches: N' in the info output to confirm it landed.

WHAT EACH GROUP DOES:
• Block_1-2 (0-9): global layout, pose, composition.
• Block_3-4 (10-19): subject rendering, anatomy, material.
• Block_5-6 (20-27): surface, texture, fine detail.
• Text_Fusion: how strongly the prompt steers the image.

ADVANCED:
• 'vectors_override' takes exactly 34 comma-separated values (28 blocks + 4 txtfusion + projector + txtmlp) and bypasses the sliders.
• Scaled-FP8 layers with a companion scale are skipped and reported - patching them would double-apply their scale.

nodes.title: 🟪🔬 Model Sub-Block Tuner ___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Same idea as the Model Tuner, one level deeper: scales a single tensor family inside the blocks you select, instead of the whole block.

HOW TO USE:
1. target_block - a group (Block_3 = 10-14) or one single block (the indented '↳' entries).
2. mode - 'Soft Value' damps to 10%, 'Real Value' is 1:1.
3. Move only the sliders you mean; 0.00 = untouched.

WHAT THE SLIDERS ARE:
• ATTN_wq/wk/wv - what the layer looks for and reads.
• ATTN_wo_out - what attention writes back.
• ATTN_gate_attn - how much attention is let through.
• MLP_gate_swiglu / up_proj / down_proj - the feed-forward stage, where most style lives.
• MOD_lin_time - timestep modulation.
• NORMS_block_scales / ATTN_qknorm_scales - 1-D norm scales, very sensitive.

TIP: chain two of these to hit two different blocks; each one clones the patcher, so they stack cleanly.

nodes.title: 🟪🌿 Model Axis Rotator___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Rotates each selected weight inside its own dominant subspace: same energy, different direction. Nothing is scaled up or down, so it changes WHAT a layer means rather than HOW LOUD it is.

HOW TO USE:
1. 'target_block' - a group or one single block. 'sub_components' narrows further.
2. 'depth_reach' - how much of the layer the rotation reaches: Light = rank 8, Default = 16, Heavy = 32.
3. Turn ONE dial at a time, +/-180 deg. Negative turns the same amount the other way.

THE FOUR DIALS:
• structural_rot_x - rotation within each component plane. The most local control, safest to start with.
• structural_rot_y - tilts a branch into the residual trunk, coupling neighbouring components.
• tensor_rot_x - long-range channel phase: couples each direction with the one half a subspace away.
• tensor_rot_y - mirrored pairwise rotation between channel pairs.

WATCH OUT: NORMS are 1-D and cannot be rotated - selecting them does nothing. Start at 5-15 deg; past ~60 deg the model usually stops being coherent.

nodes.title: 🟪🌀 Model Chaos Rotator___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Rotates each selected weight in its dominant subspace by random per-plane angles, instead of dials you choose. Same energy in, different direction out - a style drift rather than a strength change.

HOW TO USE:
1. 'target_block' and 'sub_components' - where to rotate.
2. 'depth_reach' - Light = rank 8, Default = 16, Heavy = 32.
3. 'chaos_strength' (0.0-1.0) - the maximum per-plane angle as a fraction of 90 deg. 0.35 is the default; 0.10-0.20 is a gentle drift.
4. 'harmonic_coherence' (0.0-1.0) - snaps the random angles towards multiples of 45 deg. Higher = more structured, less noisy.
5. 'seed' - a different flavour. CRC32-based, so it reproduces across ComfyUI restarts.

WATCH OUT: NORMS are 1-D and cannot be rotated. Change ONLY the seed between generations to compare flavours fairly.

nodes.title: 🟪🧭 Model Compass Rotator___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Rotates in ONE chosen direction instead of randomly: you pick a bearing on a style compass and how far to travel along it. The other two rotators give you dials and dice; this one gives you a heading.

HOW TO USE:
1. 'target_block' and 'sub_components' - where to rotate.
2. 'style_direction' (0-360 deg) - the bearing. It blends continuously between local and long-range rotation planes, so nearby values give related styles.
3. 'rotation_angle' (-90 to +90) - how far you travel. 0 = base model, 15 = gentle, 45 = distinct, 90 = maximum. Negative travels the same distance the opposite way.
4. 'manifold' - rotate the output space (what the layer emits) or the input space (what it listens to).
5. 'seed' - permutes the planes identically in every layer, so the style stays coherent across blocks.

HOW TO EXPLORE: fix everything, sweep style_direction in steps of 45 deg at rotation_angle 15. That is your map. Then increase the angle along the bearing you liked.

widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:

• structural_rot_y - tilts a branch into the residual trunk.

• tensor_rot_y - mirrored pairwise rotation between channel pairs.

WATCH OUT: be far more conservative than on the model - 5-10 deg is already a lot here. NORMS are 1-D and cannot be rotated.

3. 'chaos_strength' (0.0-1.0) - maximum per-plane angle as a fraction of 90 deg. Default 0.25; keep it low, 0.05-0.15, on the text tower.
4. 'harmonic_coherence' (0.0-1.0) - snaps angles towards 45 deg multiples. Higher = more structured.
5. 'seed' - a different reading; reproduces exactly.

WATCH OUT: the failure mode here is the prompt being ignored, not the image degrading. If adherence drops, lower chaos_strength before anything else.

nodes.title: 🟨🧭 CLIP Compass Rotator___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Rotates the CLIP layers along ONE chosen bearing instead of randomly: you pick a direction on the style compass and how far to go.

HOW TO USE:
1. 'target_layer' and 'sub_components' - where to rotate. Visual_* (36-59) is the vision tower, active only with reference images.
2. 'style_direction' (0-360 deg) - the bearing; blends between local and long-range planes, so nearby values stay related.
3. 'rotation_angle' (-90 to +90) - the distance. 0 = base, 15 = gentle, 45 = distinct. On CLIP, stay under about 20.
4. 'manifold' - output space (what the layer emits) or input space (what it listens to).
5. 'seed' - permutes planes identically in every layer, keeping the effect coherent across layers.

HOW TO EXPLORE: fixed seed and prompt, rotation_angle 10, sweep style_direction by 45 deg. Judge prompt adherence, not looks.

nodes.title: 🟨🔬 CLIP Sub-Block Tuner ___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Scales one tensor family inside the CLIP layers you select, instead of the whole layer group.

HOW TO USE:
1. target_layer - a group (Layer_3 = 10-14) or one single layer ('↳' entries). Visual_* entries (36-59) belong to the vision tower.
2. mode - 'Soft Value' damps to 10%, 'Real Value' is 1:1.
3. Move only what you mean; 0.00 = untouched.

WHAT THE SLIDERS ARE:
• ATTN_q_proj / k_proj - what the layer looks for in the prompt.
• ATTN_v_proj / o_proj - what it carries forward and writes back.
• ATTN_q_norm - query normalisation, sensitive.
• MLP_gate_proj / up_proj / down_proj - the feed-forward stage; strongest effect on how the prompt is interpreted.
• NORMS_layernorm - 1-D, tiny moves only.

TIP: test with a long, awkward prompt. Changes here show up as adherence, not as prettiness.

nodes.title: 🩷🧬 LoRA-to-5D Extractor _ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Compresses a LoRA into its N dominant SVD directions and writes a small .json 'modifier' into models/arthemy_modifiers/, for the 5D Tuners.

HOW TO USE:
1. Pick 'lora_name'. 'custom_modifier_name' is optional.
2. 'num_dimensions' (1-8): how many directions to keep. 5 is the useful default.
3. 'storage': auto (recommended) measures the fidelity a DCT would really give here and falls back to raw below 35%. raw = a few MB, exact. DCT = tens of KB, lossy.
4. 'harmonic_order' applies to DCT only.

WHY KEEP IT BYPASSED (Ctrl+B):
It is an output node, so it runs on EVERY queue and rewrites the file each time. Extract once, bypass it, then point the 5D Tuner at the .json.

nodes.title: 🟪🟨📂 Preset Loader ___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Replays a .json preset onto the model and CLIP: re-attaches the scalar and granular patches, and reproduces every recipe by re-running the node that made it.

HOW TO USE:
1. 'preset' - pick from the dropdown, or set 'custom_path' to a file or folder (it overrides the dropdown).
2. 'strength_model' / 'strength_clip' - scale everything in the preset. 1.00 = as saved, 0.50 = half, 1.50 = amplified, negative = inverted.
3. Chain more tuners after it, or feed a Visualizer to see what landed.

WATCH OUT:
• Layers carrying a scaled-FP8 companion scale are skipped and reported - patching them would double-apply the scale.
• A single malformed recipe is skipped with a warning; it no longer takes the whole preset down with it.

nodes.title: 🟪🟨 Model Baker + Model Saver | CLIP Saver
widgets_values:
WHAT THEY DO:
• Model Baker - folds every pending patch into the weights themselves, in memory. Nothing is written to disk; what comes out is a model that carries the tuning as weights, with an empty patch stack.
• Model Saver / CLIP Saver - write a full .safetensors checkpoint of the tuned model / text encoder, patches included.

HOW TO USE:
1. Baker: put it at the end of a tuner chain, before the KSampler, when the patch stack has grown long or a downstream node needs plain weights. Its 'info' reports how many tensors it actually baked.
2. Savers: set 'output_checkpoint' (the filename) and 'precision' - BF16 or FP8_E4M3. Feed them straight from the tuned MODEL / CLIP: they already read patched weights, so there is no need to bake first.

WATCH OUT:
• Baking is one-way for the session. The Reset Patcher cannot undo it, because baked weights ARE the weights.
• Scaled-FP8 layers carrying a companion scale are NOT baked - fusing them would double-apply that scale. The Baker reports them and leaves their patches attached; the Savers handle them correctly by folding the scale into the weight.
• Both Savers are output nodes: they run on EVERY queue and rewrite the file, even with 'saved_path' unconnected. Bypass them (Ctrl+B) once you have the checkpoint.
• LoRAs are never stored in presets - baking or saving is how you make them permanent.

nodes.title: 🟪🌪️ Model Sub-Block Chaos Tuner ___ README
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Perturbs chosen tensor families with reproducible pseudo-random noise, to find variations you would not dial in by hand.

HOW TO USE:
1. target_block - a group or one single block.
2. chaos_strength - how strong the perturbation is (default 0.10). Start there.
3. Chance sliders (0.0-1.0) - the probability that each family gets perturbed. 0.0 = never.
4. seed - change it to draw a different variation. Same seed always gives the same result, across ComfyUI restarts.

tune_mode:
• 'Block-Level' - one draw per tensor, coherent.
• 'Element-Level (Sub-atomic)' - per-element noise, much rougher.

WATCH OUT: the roll happens once per module, so paired tensors are never split apart. High chance on MLP families changes texture fastest.

nodes.title: 🟪📊 Channel Magnitude Tuner
widgets_values:
WHAT IT DOES:
• Ranks the residual-stream channels (d_model, 6144 on Krea-2) by how much energy each one carries, cuts them into 12 logarithmic bands, and scales each band by its slider.
• A vertical cut: not 'which block', but 'which channels', across the whole model at once.

HOW TO USE:
1. 'channel_scope' - which sub-network the gain lands on. MLP (default) is where the interesting part of a tuning lives; ATTN for the attention projections.
2. 'channel_path' - Both (default) applies the gain where the sub-network reads from the residual AND where it writes back. Reads only shifts what it listens to: better prompt adherence, about half the effect on an MLP. Writes only is a plain output gain, weakest.
3. 'mode' - Soft damps the slider to 10%, Real is 1:1.
4. Move ONE band at a time. Band_01 = the top 1% of channels (macro structure, subjects). Band_12 = the quietest 18% (fine grain, micro-texture).

GOOD TO KNOW:
• The ranking is profiled from the checkpoint and cached in models/arthemy_profiles/: the first move costs 15-25 s, every one after is instant.
• It survives a preset - the band values are saved as a recipe.

nodes.title: HOW TO USE THIS WORKFLOW
widgets_values:
1. Pick your tools: Explore the "Tools" area below to find every node in this suite alongside a quick summary of what it does.

2. Build your chain: Copy and paste any combination of tuning nodes into your workspace, chaining them directly between the Reset Patcher and the Visualizers (Model Visualizer / CLIP Visualizer).

3. Save your result: Once you achieve the look you want:
• Save a Preset (Preset Saver) for a lightweight, reusable recipe, or
• Bake a Checkpoint (Model Baker / Model Saver) to fold changes permanently into model weights.

Tip — Presets are modular: You can always load an existing preset with Preset Loader, stack additional tuning nodes on top of it, and save the result as a new version.

<---- Yes, YOU CAN DELETE THIS PRESET LOADER, it was just made to showcase the effect.
